Rashi on Pesachim 24b:10:1.hebrew: כלאי הכרם - כתיב (דברים כ״ב:ט׳): "פן תקדש המלאה", דמשמע: לא תהנה ממנו אלא תשרפנו; ופן — לאו הוא:
Rashi on Pesachim 24b:10:1.english: Diverse kinds of the vineyard - It is written (Deuteronomy 22:9): "Lest the fullness become forfeit," which implies: You may not derive benefit from it, but rather you must burn it; and "lest" is a negative prohibition.

Rashi on Pesachim 24b:11:1.english: That it is prohibited - In eating.

Rashi on Pesachim 24b:12:1.english: Orlah, through which no sin was committed - In its planting.

Rashi on Pesachim 24b:12:2.hebrew: בשר בחלב שנעבדה בו עבירה - כשבישלו, ועבר עליו על לאו "לא תבשל":
Rashi on Pesachim 24b:12:2.english: Meat in milk, through which a sin has been committed - When one cooked it and violated regarding it the negative commandment "You shall not cook."

Rashi on Pesachim 24b:1:1.hebrew: צירעה - שרץ העוף היא, וגם שורצת על הארץ, ויש בה אלו חמש לאוין, ומוסיף עליה לאו דשרץ העוף במשנה תורה (יד): "וכל שרץ העוף טמא הוא לכם לא יאכלו". שרץ — לשון רחוש ונענוע ואינו נראה, ואין בהמה וחיה הגבוהין מן הארץ בכלל שרץ. הלכך, "לא תשקצו את נפשותיכם בבהמה ובעוף וגו'" דכתיב בקדושים תהיו — אינו מן המנין, דלאו בשרצים כתיב:
Rashi on Pesachim 24b:1:1.english: A hornet - It is a winged swarming creature, and it also swarms upon the ground, and these five negative prohibitions apply to it, and [the Torah] adds to it the negative prohibition of a winged swarming creature in Mishneh Torah (Deuteronomy 14:19): "And every winged swarming creature is unclean to you; they shall not be eaten." Sheretz [swarming creature] is a term for creeping and swaying movement that is not [clearly] visible, and domesticated beasts and wild animals, which are raised above the ground, are not included in [the category of] sheretz. Therefore, "You shall not make your souls detestable by beast or by fowl, etc." (Leviticus 20:25), which is written in [Parashat] Kedoshim Tiheyu, is not included in the count, because it is not written regarding swarming creatures.

Rashi on Pesachim 24b:2:1.hebrew: והבשר למה לי - השתא דאמר': קרא לאו לגופיה אתא, אלא לאם אינו ענין — תינח "ואשר יגע בכל טמא לא יאכל", "והבשר" למה לי? ומשני: לרבות עצים ולבונה לקבל טומאה, ואע"ג דלאו אוכלא הוא:
Rashi on Pesachim 24b:2:1.english: Why do I need "And the flesh" - Now that you have said [that the] verse did not come for its own sake, but rather for [the principle of] "if it does not apply to its own matter" — granted [the words] "and that which touches any impure thing shall not be eaten," [but] why do I need "And the flesh"? And [the Gemara] answers: To include wood and frankincense to contract ritual impurity, even though they are not food.

Rashi on Pesachim 24b:2:2.hebrew: והבשר כל טהור יאכל למה לי - והבשר יתירה מבעיא ליה, דאילו "כל טהור יאכל בשר" דריש ליה במנחות (ד' כה:): "כל טהור יאכל בשר והנפש אשר תאכל בשר וגו' — הניתר לטהורין חייבין עליו משום טומאה, יצא בשר שנטמא לפני זריקת דם". לשון אחר: בין ברישא בין בסיפא, ו' יתירא מיבעי' ליה:
Rashi on Pesachim 24b:2:2.english: "And as for the flesh, every one that is pure may eat" — why do I need [this] - [The Gemara] is asking about the superfluous [word] "and the flesh"; for as for "every one that is pure may eat flesh," it is expounded in Menachot (25b): "Every one that is pure may eat flesh, and the soul that eats of the flesh, etc." — that which is permitted to pure [people] entails liability on its account for [eating it in a state of] impurity, excluding meat that became impure before the sprinkling of the blood. Another explanation: Both in the first clause and in the second clause, it is asking about the superfluous [letter] vav.

Rashi on Pesachim 24b:3:1.hebrew: לרבות את האימורין - שאם נטמאו ואכלן טהור, שיעבור עליהן משום ב' לאוין: לאו דזרות — שאף הכהן זר אצלם — ולאו דטומאת בשר. ואדלעיל קאי, והכי קאמר: לא יאכל, והבשר נמי שנטמא — לא יאכל:
Rashi on Pesachim 24b:3:1.english: To include the sacrificial parts - That if they became impure and a ritually pure person ate them, he violates two negative prohibitions on their account: the negative prohibition of zarut [consumption by an unauthorized person] — for even a priest is an outsider with respect to them — and the negative prohibition of [eating] impure meat. And [this] refers back to what is stated above, and this is what it means: [Flesh that touches any impure thing] shall not be eaten, and this flesh as well, if it became impure, shall not be eaten.

Rashi on Pesachim 24b:3:2.hebrew: אשר לה' - קרא יתירה הוא, דה"ל למכתב "מזבח השלמים וטומאתו עליו", וכתיב "אשר לה'", לרבות אף בשר הקרב לה', שאם אכלו בטומאה ענוש כרת. ומשני: התם בטומאת הגוף איירי, והאי "וטומאתו עליו" מוקמינן לה בזבחים בפרק ב"ש (זבחים דף מג:) בטומאת הגוף הכתוב מדבר, והכא רבינהו לאזהרת טומאת בשר — כשנטמאו הם והוא טהור — שיהא מוזהר עליהן. והכא ליכא כרת אלא לאו, דאימעט מכרת בזבחים בפרק ב"ש:
Rashi on Pesachim 24b:3:2.english: Which belong to the Lord - This is a superfluous verse, for it should have written: “from the sacrifice of peace-offerings, and his impurity is upon him,” yet it is written: “which belong to the Lord,” to include even meat that is offered to the Lord, so that if one ate it in a state of impurity, he is punished with karet. And the Gemara answers: There it is dealing with impurity of the body, and this phrase, “and his impurity is upon him,” we establish in Zevachim in the chapter entitled Beit Shammai (Zevachim 43b), that Scripture is speaking of impurity of the body; and here it included them for the prohibition of impurity of meat, when they became impure and he is pure, that he should be prohibited concerning them. And here there is no karet, but rather a negative prohibition, as it was excluded from karet in Zevachim in the chapter entitled Beit Shammai.

Rashi on Pesachim 24b:5:1.english: Only in the manner of their consumption - Unless he ate them in the manner of their consumption.

Rashi on Pesachim 24b:6:1.hebrew: איכא דאמרי - הא דרבי אבהו אהנאה איתמר, ואהנך דאסירי בהנאה:
Rashi on Pesachim 24b:6:1.english: Some say - This [statement] of Rabbi Abbahu was stated regarding benefit, and regarding those [items] that are forbidden from [deriving] benefit.

Rashi on Pesachim 24b:6:2.hebrew: חלב - אין דרך הנאתו אלא בהבערה ולמשוח עורות, ולא לרפואה; וכ"ש אוכל חלב חי:
Rashi on Pesachim 24b:6:2.english: Fat - The usual manner of its benefit is only for kindling and to grease hides, and not for medicine; and all the more so [regarding] one who eats raw fat.

Rashi on Pesachim 24b:8:1.hebrew: אין סופגין את הארבעים כו' - גבי משקין קאי במסכת תרומות, וקאמר דאין כל מי פירות קרויין משקין אלא אלו בלבד. אין סופגין את הארבעים על שום מי פירות של ערלה, משום דבכולהו שלא כדרך הנאתן הוא, אלא אלו:
Rashi on Pesachim 24b:8:1.english: One does not absorb the forty [lashes], etc. - [This teaching] is stated regarding liquids in Tractate Terumot, and it says that not all fruit juices are called liquids, but only these. One does not absorb the forty [lashes] for any fruit juice of orlah, because with all [the others] it is not in their usual manner of [deriving] benefit, except for these.

Rashi on Pesachim 24b:9:1.hebrew: בשלמא אי אשמעינן בפרי גופא - דאי אכיל שלא כדרכו — כגון שבישל אגוזים או אפרסקין ואכלן — ואשמעינן דלא מחייב:
Rashi on Pesachim 24b:9:1.english: Granted, if it taught us about the fruit itself - That if he ate [it] not in its [usual] manner — such as if he cooked nuts or peaches and ate them — and [the mishna] taught us that he is not liable.

Rashi on Pesachim 24b:9:2.hebrew: שפיר - שמעינן מינה דאין לוקין אלא כדרך אכילתן; אבל השתא, טעמא דפטור משום דלאו פרי אכל:
Rashi on Pesachim 24b:9:2.english: [It would work out] well - We would learn from it that one is flogged only [when eating] in the usual manner of their consumption; but now, the reason that he is exempt is because he did not eat fruit.

Tosafot on Pesachim 24b:10:1.hebrew: (לעיל) הכל מודים בכלאי הכרם - הא דלא קאמר "הכל מודים בחולין שנשחטו בעזרה" — משום דכתיב בהו אכילה, דמוזבחת ואכלת נפקא לן; ועוד, דאיכא מאן דאמר לאו דאורייתא. והא דלא קאמר "הכל מודים בבשר וחלב" — שמא משום דאין מזהירין מן הדין:
Tosafot on Pesachim 24b:10:1.english: (Above) "All concede with regard to diverse kinds of the vineyard" - That which [Abaye] did not say, "All concede with regard to non-sacred animals slaughtered in the [Temple] courtyard" — [this is] because eating is written concerning them, as we derive [the prohibition] from "and you shall slaughter... and you shall eat"; and furthermore, there is an authority who says [that this prohibition] is not from the Torah. And that which [Abaye] did not say, "All concede with regard to meat [cooked] in milk" — perhaps [it is] because one does not derive a warning from an a fortiori deduction [and thus lashes cannot be administered].

Tosafot on Pesachim 24b:12:1.hebrew: אמרת קל וחומר - תימה: היכי אלים ק"ו לאפוקי מג"ש, דנילף מנבילה בג"ש שלא תאסר בהנאה כמו נבילה? ובפרק כל הבשר (חולין קטז.) איכא תנא דיליף הכי, וסבר דבשר בחלב לא אסור בהנאה. ואור"ת, דבההוא קרא דאנשי קדש כתיב ביה נמי איסורי הנאה, דמבשר בשדה דרשינן קדשים שיצאו חוץ למחיצה; וגלי לן ק"ו דגמרינן מקדשים ולא (מנבילה). וא"ת: בלא ק"ו נמי מקשינן לחומרא? וי"ל, דהכא ס"ד לאקשויי לקולא, משום דמפורש בהדיא בקרא היתר הנאה, דכתיב: "לכלב תשליכון אותו". הקשה הר"י דאורלינ"ש: אמאי לא ילפינן מנותר איסור אכילה ואיסור הנאה מקדש קדש, דמההוא קדש דנותר דריש ג"ש בפ' לולב וערבה (סוכה מט.) ובפרק כל הזבחים (זבחים כח:)? וי"ל, דהכא "עם קדוש" מ"אנשי קדש" דרשי', שהן ענין אחד, דקיימא קדושה אגברי. אי נמי: דנין חולין מחולין, ואין דנין חולין מקדשים:
Tosafot on Pesachim 24b:12:1.english: You may state an a fortiori inference - [This is] puzzling: How is an a fortiori [inference] powerful [enough] to override a gezeirah shavah, such that we should derive from neveilah via a gezeirah shavah that it should not be prohibited in benefit, just like neveilah? And in the chapter [entitled] Kol HaBasar (Chullin 116a), there is a Tanna who derives this way, and maintains that meat in milk is not prohibited in benefit. And Rabbeinu Tam says that in that [same] verse of “men of holiness” (Exodus 22:30), prohibitions of benefit are also written in it, for from [the words] “flesh in the field” we expound sacrificial meat that went outside the boundary [which is prohibited to derive benefit from]; and the a fortiori [inference] reveals to us that we learn from sacrificial meat and not from [neveilah]. And if you say: Even without an a fortiori [inference], we would also compare [it] to the stringency [i.e., to sacrificial meat]! And one can say: Here, it would enter your mind to compare [it] to the leniency, because the permission of benefit is explicitly stated in the verse, as it is written: “You shall cast it to the dogs” (Exodus 22:30). The Ri of Orleans questioned: Why do we not derive both the prohibition of eating and the prohibition of benefit from notar, from [the common word] “holy” [and] “holy”? For from that [word] “holy” in [the passage regarding] notar, [the Gemara] expounds a gezeirah shavah in the chapter [entitled] Lulav VeAravah (Sukkah 49a) and in the chapter [entitled] Kol HaZevachim (Zevachim 28b)! And one can say: Here, we expound “sacred people” (Deuteronomy 14:21) from “sacred men” (Exodus 22:30), which are one concept, as the sanctity pertains to the people. Alternatively: One derives non-sacred [matters] from non-sacred [matters], and one does not derive non-sacred [matters] from consecrated [matters].

Tosafot on Pesachim 24b:12:2.hebrew: אמרת ק"ו - איסור אכילה לא מצי למילף בק"ו מערלה, כדאמר בכל הבשר (חולין קטו:), משום דאיכא למימר: חורש בשור וחמור וחוסם פרה יוכיח, דנעבדה בהו עבירה, ושרו באכילה. אבל השתא דיליף מקרא איסור אכילה, ליכא למימר תוכיח — דהנהו שרו באכילה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 24b:12:2.english: "You may state an a fortiori inference" - The prohibition against eating could not be derived via an a fortiori inference from orla, as [the Gemara] says in [the chapter entitled] "Kol HaBasar" (Chullin 115b), because one could say: [The case of one who] plows with an ox and a donkey, and [one who] muzzles a cow, proves [otherwise], for a transgression was committed with them, and [yet] they are permitted to be eaten. However, now that [the Gemara] derives the prohibition against eating from Scripture, one cannot say "[they] prove [otherwise]" — because those [cases] are permitted to be eaten.

Tosafot on Pesachim 24b:1:1.hebrew: צירעה לוקה שש - פ"ה, דהא דכתיב בקדושים: "אל תשקצו את נפשותיכם בבהמה ובעוף ובכל אשר תרמוש האדמה" וגו' — לא חשיב ליה, דבגדולים מיירי, דלא כתיב שרץ; ולשון שרץ — דבר שהוא נד בארץ ואינו נראה אלא ע"י שירוצו, מפני קטנו. וקשה, דבפ' ד' מיתות (סנהדרין נט:) דרשינן: "וכל חיה הרומשת" — זה הנחש, משמע דרמישה הוה נמי בדבר הרוחש, כמו נחש שהולך על גחונו! ותי' הר"י דאורלינ"ש, דההוא קרא איירי בח' שרצים, דאמרינן במעילה בפרק קדשי מזבח (מעילה דף טז: ושם): "במובדלים ממך דיבר הכתוב", דכתיב בסיפא דקרא: "אשר הבדלתי לכם לטמא", והיינו ח' שרצים שהן טמאים:
Tosafot on Pesachim 24b:1:1.english: [For eating] a hornet, [he] is flogged with six [sets of lashes] - Rashi explained that that which is written in [Parashat] Kedoshim: “You shall not make your souls detestable with beast, or with bird, or with anything that creeps on the ground...” (Leviticus 20:25) — he did not count it, because it is dealing with large [creatures], as [the word] sheretz [creeping creature] is not written [there]; and the term sheretz [denotes] an entity that moves upon the ground and is discernible only through its scurrying, due to its smallness. And this is difficult, for in the chapter [entitled] Arba Mitot (Sanhedrin 59b), we expound: “And every living creature that creeps [haromeshet]” (Genesis 1:28) — this is the serpent; which implies that creeping [remisah] also applies to a crawling creature, like a snake, which goes upon its belly! And the Ri of Orléans answered that that verse is dealing with the eight swarming creatures, for we say in Meilah, in the chapter [entitled] Kodshei Mizbe'ach (Meilah 16b and there): “The verse speaks of those that are set apart from you,” as it is written at the end of the verse: “Which I have set apart for you as impure” (Leviticus 20:25) — and that refers to the eight swarming creatures, which are [ritually] impure.

Tosafot on Pesachim 24b:3:1.hebrew: לרבות את האימורים - דסד"א: אין חייבין עליהם משום טומאה, הואיל ואין ניתרים, ודרשינן במנחות בפרק הקומץ את המנחה (דף כה:): ״הניתר לטהורי' חייבים עליהם משום טומאה״ — להכי איצטריך לרבויינהו. מיהו קשה, דבמעילה בפ' חטאת העוף (מעילה דף י:) דריש התם: ״מאשר יקרב״ — בכל הקדשים הכתוב מדבר, ויליף התם אימורים וכל שאין ניתר לטהורים! ורבינו שמשון תירץ, דאיצטריך לרבויי, דסד"א דלא יבא איסור טומאה ויחול על איסור חלב:
Tosafot on Pesachim 24b:3:1.english: “To include the sacrificial parts” - For you might have thought that one is not liable for them on account of ritual impurity, since they do not become permitted [for consumption] — and we expound in Menachot in the chapter [entitled] Hakometz Et Haminchah (25b): “[Only for] that which is permitted to pure people is one liable on account of ritual impurity” — therefore, it was necessary to include them. However, this is difficult, for in Meilah, in the chapter [entitled] Chatat HaOf (Meilah 10b), [the Gemara] expounds there: From “[whoever he be... that] approaches” (Leviticus 22:3) — the verse speaks of all consecrated items, and it derives there [liability for] sacrificial parts and anything that does not become permitted to pure people! And Rabbeinu Shimshon answered that it was necessary to include [them here], because you might have thought that the prohibition of ritual impurity should not come and take effect upon the prohibition of forbidden fat [chelev].

Tosafot on Pesachim 24b:6:1.hebrew: פרט לאוכל חלב חי - והא דאמר בגיד הנשה (חולין קב:): "אכל צפור טהורה בחייה — בכל שהוא, במיתתה — בכזית" — שאני עוף, שהוא רך וחזי לאומצא, וחשיב כדרך הנאתו. והא דאמר בהקומץ רבה (מנחות כא.): "דם שבשלו — אינו עובר עליו", ופריך אביי מהא דתניא: "הקפה את הדם ואכלו, או שהמחה את החלב וגמעו — חייב", ומשני: "כאן שהקפה באור, וכאן שהקפה בחמה" — ולפי הך דהכא, צ"ל שהברייתא לצדדים קתני: הקפה את הדם בחמה, ואת החלב באור; דאי בחמה — חי הוא, ופטור:
Tosafot on Pesachim 24b:6:1.english: To exclude one who eats raw fat - And as for that which is said in [the chapter] Gid HaNasheh (Chullin 102b): "[If] one ate a kosher bird while it was alive, [he is liable] for any amount; [if he ate it] after its death, [he is liable only] for an olive's bulk" — a bird is different, as it is tender and fit to be eaten raw, and [so eating it this way] is considered in the usual manner of deriving benefit from it. And as for that which is said in [the chapter] Hakometz Rabbah (Menachot 21a): "Blood that one cooked, one does not transgress [the prohibition of blood] on its account," and Abaye objected from that which is taught [in a baraita]: "If one congealed blood and ate it, or melted fat and gulped it down, he is liable," and [the Gemara] answers: "Here, where he congealed it by fire; and there, where he congealed it in the sun" — according to this [passage] here, one must say that the baraita teaches disjunctively: he congealed the blood in the sun, and [melted] the fat by fire; for if [the fat were melted] in the sun, it is raw, and [he is] exempt.

Tosafot on Pesachim 24b:9:1.hebrew: אלא הכא משום דזיעה בעלמא הוא - תימה לר"י, דבהעור והרוטב (חולין קכא. ושם) יליף מקרא דאין חייב משום ערלה אלא על היוצא מזיתים וענבים, דגמר ערלה "פרי" "פרי" מבכורים, ובכורים מתרומה, ובתרומה כתיב "תירוש ויצהר" — אם כן, אמאי איצטריך למימר הכא "זיעה בעלמא הוא"? וי"ל, דהא דאיצטריך למילף התם "פרי" "פרי" מבכורים — לאו למעוטי שאר משקין איצטריך; דמן הדין, אפילו תירוש ויצהר לא היה ליחשב למשקין פרי, דזיעה בעלמא הוא, כדאמרינן הכא, והתם איצטריך למילף שנחשוב משקה של תירוש ויצהר כמו הפרי. והשתא א"ש הא דאמר בשמעתין דזיעה בעלמא הוא, דמהאי טעמא הוא דשמעינן דמשקה אינו כפרי. מיהו תימה: אמאי אמר דזיעה בעלמא הוא? והא טעם כעיקר דאורייתא:
Tosafot on Pesachim 24b:9:1.english: “Rather, here, because it is merely moisture” - The Ri finds it astonishing: For in [the chapter entitled] HaOhr VehaRotev (Chullin 121a and there), [the Gemara] derives from Scripture that one is liable on account of orlah only for that which emerges from olives and grapes, as it derives orlah [through the verbal analogy of] “fruit” [and] “fruit” from first fruits, and first fruits from terumah, and regarding terumah it is written: “wine and oil” — if so, why was it necessary to say here [that] “it is merely moisture”? And one can say that that which it was necessary to derive there [by] “fruit” [and] “fruit” from first fruits was not needed to exclude other liquids; for by strict law, even wine and oil should not have been considered fruit liquids, as [liquid] is merely moisture, as we say here, and there it was necessary to derive [from Scripture] that we should consider the liquid of wine and oil like the fruit [itself]. And now, that which is said in our passage, that “it is merely moisture,” works out well, for it is from this reason that we learn that liquid is not like fruit. However, it is [still] astonishing: Why did [Abaye] say that it is merely moisture? But isn't [the rule that] flavor is like the substance [itself] of Torah origin?
